questions.question: If {x² + y² − 16x + 38y + 425 = 0}, then the value of {x² + y²} is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Rewrite the equation by **completing the squares** for both x and y terms.

x² − 16x + 64 + y² + 38y + 361 = 0 since 64 + 361 = 425.

This gives (x − 8)² + (y + 19)² = 0.

For **real numbers**, the sum of squares is zero only if x = 8 and y = −19.

Then x² + y² = 8² + (−19)² = 64 + 361 = 425.

**∴ The correct answer is 425.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x² + y² − 16x + 38y + 425 = 0

**Formula Used:** (a ± b)² = a² ± 2ab + b²

**Calculations:**

⇒ (x² − 16x) + (y² + 38y) + 425 = 0

⇒ (x² − 2 × x × 8 + 8² − 64) + (y² + 2 × y × 19 + 19² − 361) + 425 = 0

⇒ (x − 8)² − 64 + (y + 19)² − 361 + 425 = 0

⇒ (x − 8)² + (y + 19)² − 425 + 425 = 0

⇒ (x − 8)² + (y + 19)² = 0

⇒ For real variables, a sum of squares is 0 only if each square is 0: x − 8 = 0 and y + 19 = 0

⇒ x = 8 and y = −19

⇒ Required value: x² + y² = 8² + (−19)²

⇒ x² + y² = 64 + 361 = 425

**∴ The correct answer is 425.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sum of Squares Property

For any real numbers A, B, and C, if A² + B² + C² + ... = 0, then A = 0, B = 0, C = 0, etc.

Perfect Square Trinomial

The expression x² + kx becomes a perfect square by adding (k/2)², resulting in (x + k/2)².

Geometric Interpretation

The equation (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r² represents a circle; if r = 0, it represents a single point (h, k).</p

questions.question: Public health services remained largely inaccessible to the masses during the colonial rule. What was India's approximate life expectancy at the time of independence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30-32 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India’s life expectancy at the time of independence in 1947 was approximately **30-32 years**.
 
• The low life expectancy was attributed to widespread poverty, lack of healthcare facilities, and high prevalence of infectious diseases like malaria, cholera, and tuberculosis.
 
• During the colonial era, public health services were **highly inadequate**, especially in rural areas, leading to high mortality rates.
 
• Infant mortality and maternal mortality rates were also alarmingly high due to poor medical infrastructure and lack of proper nutrition.
 
• Post-independence, significant improvements in healthcare and living standards contributed to a gradual increase in life expectancy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Life Expectancy:** It refers to the average number of years a person is expected to live, based on demographic factors like healthcare, sanitation, and nutrition.
 
• **Colonial Healthcare System:** During British rule, healthcare was largely focused on protecting the colonial administration and urban elites, leaving the rural population underserved.
 
• **Post-Independence Initiatives:** India introduced major public health programs such as the National Malaria Eradication Program (1953) and family planning initiatives to improve public health metrics.
 
• **Current Trends:** As of 2023, India’s life expectancy has increased to approximately **69-70 years**, reflecting advancements in healthcare and living conditions.
 
• **Global Comparison:** In 1947, India’s life expectancy was among the lowest globally, but consistent efforts in healthcare have significantly improved its ranking over the decades.

questions.question: Which Schedule and Article contain the names and extent of states and union territories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First Schedule – Articles 1 and 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **First Schedule** of the Indian Constitution contains the **names and territorial extent of States and Union Territories**.
 
• It is referenced in **Articles 1 and 4** of the Constitution.
 
• Article 1 declares India as a "Union of States" and provides for the classification of its territories into states, union territories, and other areas.
 
• Article 4 specifies the legislative process for changes in the names, boundaries, or formation of States and Union Territories, linking directly to the First Schedule.
 
• The First Schedule is periodically updated to reflect changes in state boundaries or new additions (e.g., Telangana in 2014).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 1 of the Constitution:**

 
 
• Defines India as a "Union of States."
 
• Describes the classification of territories into States, Union Territories, and other areas.
 
 
 
• **Article 4 of the Constitution:**
 
 
• Empowers Parliament to make laws for the admission or establishment of new States or altering the boundaries of existing States.
 
• Such laws are not considered constitutional amendments under Article 368.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the First Schedule:**
 
 
• It provides the official names and territorial descriptions of all States and Union Territories.
 
• It is amended whenever there are changes in state boundaries (e.g., creation of new States like Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, and Jharkhand in 2000).
 
 
 
• **Examples of Amendments:**
 
 
• The Andhra Pradesh Reorganization Act, 2014, led to the creation of Telangana, updating the First Schedule.
 
• Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh were added as Union Territories under the Jammu & Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019.

questions.question: Which type of legislative bills must be introduced in the Lok Sabha only after obtaining the prior approval of the President of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Money Bills** must be introduced in the Lok Sabha exclusively, as per Article 110 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The prior approval of the President of India is mandatory for the introduction of Money Bills in the Lok Sabha.
 
• Money Bills include provisions related to taxation, borrowing of money, expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, and other financial matters.
 
• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha holds the authority to certify whether a bill is a Money Bill or not.
 
• The Rajya Sabha can only recommend amendments to Money Bills but cannot reject or amend them directly; the Lok Sabha has the final say.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 110:** Defines Money Bills and specifies the matters it can include, such as imposition, abolition, or alteration of taxes, regulation of borrowing, and appropriation of funds.
 
• **Difference between Money Bills and Financial Bills:** Financial Bills deal with broader financial matters but are not exclusively categorized under Article 110, requiring a different legislative process.
 
• **Role of the President:** The President’s recommendation is essential for Money Bills because they involve financial implications for the government.
 
• **Speaker's Certification:** The Speaker of the Lok Sabha’s certification is conclusive and cannot be questioned in any court of law.
 
• **Rajya Sabha's Role:** The Rajya Sabha has limited authority over Money Bills and can only recommend changes within a 14-day window, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.

questions.question: Find roots of {x² + (2a + 3)x + (a² + 3a) = 0.}​
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **Quadratic Equation** of the form x² + (u + v)x + uv = 0, the roots are simply −u and −v.

Compare this with the given equation: x² + (2a + 3)x + (a² + 3a) = 0.

Rewrite the constant term: a² + 3a = a(a + 3). Here, u = a and v = a + 3.

Check the middle term: u + v = a + (a + 3) = 2a + 3, which matches the coefficient of x.

The roots are −a and −(a + 3) ⇒ −a and −a − 3.

**∴ The correct answer is {x = −a, −a − 3}.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x² + (2a + 3)x + (a² + 3a) = 0

**Method:** Factorization of the **Quadratic Equation** by splitting the middle term.

⇒ x² + (2a + 3)x + a(a + 3) = 0

⇒ x² + ax + (a + 3)x + a(a + 3) = 0

⇒ x(x + a) + (a + 3)(x + a) = 0

⇒ (x + a)(x + a + 3) = 0

⇒ x + a = 0 or x + a + 3 = 0

⇒ x = −a or x = −(a + 3)

⇒ x = −a or x = −a − 3

**∴ The correct answer is {x = −a, −a − 3}.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Form of Quadratic Equation

A quadratic equation is expressed as ax² + bx + c = 0, where a ≠ 0.

Sum and Product of Roots

For ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is −b/a and the product of roots is c/a.

Quadratic Formula

Roots can be found using x = [−b ± √(b² − 4ac)] / 2a.

Nature of Roots

The term D = b² − 4ac is the **Discriminant**. If D > 0, roots are real and distinct; if D = 0, roots are real and equal.</p

questions.question: The simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2,200 at the rate of 7% per annum in 2 years is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net **Simple Interest** percentage = Rate × Time

Effective **Rate** = 7% × 2 = 14%

**Simple Interest** = 14% of ₹2,200

SI = 14 × 22 = 308

**∴ The correct answer is ₹308.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Principal (P)** = ₹2,200

**Rate (R)** = 7% per annum

**Time (T)** = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/481d6b56d5450c6e2419077aa41349f696b80c145e229e0172b95ea652ea400e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (2200 × 7 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 22 × 14

⇒ SI = ₹308

**∴ The correct answer is ₹308.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount

The total sum of money payable at the end of the period is calculated as **Amount = Principal + Simple Interest**.

Compound Interest (CI)

Unlike SI, **Compound Interest** is calculated on the principal and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods. Formula: A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ.

SI vs CI Relationship

For the first year, when interest is compounded annually, the **Simple Interest** is exactly equal to the **Compound Interest**.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is used to represent the ASCII value of the uppercase letter 'B'?

__
 
• ASCII stands for **American Standard Code for Information Interchange**, a character encoding standard used in computers and electronic devices.
 
• Each character in the ASCII table is assigned a unique numeric code ranging from **0 to 127**, enabling efficient communication between devices.
 
• The uppercase letter 'B' corresponds to the ASCII value **66**.
 
• In the ASCII table, uppercase letters are sequentially assigned values from **65 ('A')** to **90 ('Z')**.

• Printable characters include letters, digits, punctuation marks, and special symbols.
 
 
 
• **Control Characters:**
 
 
• Control characters, such as 10 (Line Feed) and 13 (Carriage Return), are used to control text formatting.
 
 
 
• **Extended ASCII:**
 
 
• Beyond the standard 0-127 range, extended ASCII includes codes from 128-255, primarily used for additional symbols and characters.
 
 
 
• **Application of ASCII:**
 
 
• Widely used in programming languages such as C, Python, and Java for handling text and characters.
 
• Enables interoperability across devices and systems by standardizing character representation.

questions.question: The average weight of 5 students is 60 kg. After a new student joins the group, the average becomes 62 kg. What is the weight of the new student?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Initial average** of 5 students = 60 kg

**Increase** in average after 1 new student = 62 − 60 = 2 kg

**Total students** now = 6

**Weight of new student** = Old Average + (Increase × New Total Students)

⇒ Weight = 60 + (2 × 6) = 60 + 12 = 72 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 72 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of 5 students = 60 kg

Average weight of 6 students = 62 kg

**Formula:** Total Weight = Average × Number of Students

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/81aa4a8bc0680a052f9652386aea8f605cd54c90d6cb2c7112415dfa275bb33c.png] 

⇒ Total weight of 5 students = 5 × 60 = 300 kg

⇒ Total weight of 6 students (including new one) = 6 × 62 = 372 kg

⇒ Weight of the new student = Total weight of 6 students − Total weight of 5 students

⇒ Weight = 372 − 300 = 72 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 72 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Average Formula

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Number of observations.

Net Change in Average

If every value in a set is increased by 'k', the average also increases by 'k'.

Inclusion/Exclusion Rule

New Value = New Average + (Number of previous items × Change in Average).</p

questions.question: When did the citizenship provisions in the Constitution come into effect?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The citizenship provisions as outlined in Part II of the Indian Constitution came into effect on **November 26, 1949**, coinciding with the enforcement of the Constitution of India.
 
• January 26, 1950, is celebrated as **Republic Day** in India, marking the transition of India into a sovereign democratic republic.
 
• Article 5 to Article 11 in the Constitution of India specifically deals with citizenship provisions at the time of commencement of the Constitution.
 
• The provision for citizenship was crucial for determining the legal status of individuals residing in India after independence and partition.
 
• The Constitution provides for a single citizenship for the entire country, which means that all Indians are citizens of India irrespective of the state or territory they reside in.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 5:** Defines citizenship for individuals domiciled in India at the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• **Article 6:** Grants citizenship to individuals who migrated to India from Pakistan before July 19, 1948, under specific conditions.
 
• **Article 7:** Provides citizenship for individuals who migrated to Pakistan but later returned to India under a permit for resettlement.
 
• **Article 9:** States that individuals voluntarily acquiring citizenship of another country will cease to be Indian citizens.

questions.question: 4 chairs and 4 tables cost ₹7,000 and 6 chairs and 5 tables cost ₹8,800. What is the cost of 16 chairs and 2 tables?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

From the first condition, 4 chairs + 4 tables = ₹7,000 ⇒ 1 chair + 1 table = ₹1,750.

Given 6 chairs + 5 tables = ₹8,800, we can write this as: 5(1 chair + 1 table) + 1 chair = ₹8,800.

Substituting the value: 5 × 1,750 + 1 chair = ₹8,800 ⇒ 8,750 + 1 chair = ₹8,800 ⇒ 1 chair = ₹50.

Then, 1 table = 1,750 − 50 = ₹1,700.

Cost of 16 chairs and 2 tables = 16 × 50 + 2 × 1,700 = 800 + 3,400 = ₹4,200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,200.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of 4 **chairs** (C) and 4 **tables** (T) = ₹7,000

Cost of 6 **chairs** and 5 **tables** = ₹8,800

**Formula Used:**

Method of **Elimination** for solving **simultaneous linear equations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/988a8c996b6258077fc40a23bd4159ea57ad1a81b33de46735b12e557738cb8c.png] 

Let the cost of one **chair** be C and one **table** be T.

⇒ 4C + 4T = 7,000 — (1)

⇒ 6C + 5T = 8,800 — (2)

Divide equation (1) by 4:

⇒ C + T = 1,750 — (3)

Multiply equation (3) by 5:

⇒ 5C + 5T = 8,750 — (4)

Subtract equation (4) from equation (2):

⇒ (6C + 5T) − (5C + 5T) = 8,800 − 8,750

⇒ C = 50

Substitute C = 50 in equation (3):

⇒ 50 + T = 1,750 ⇒ T = 1,700

Cost of 16 chairs and 2 tables:

⇒ 16 × 50 + 2 × 1,700

⇒ 800 + 3,400 = 4,200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,200.**

**__Additional Information__**

Elimination Method

A technique to solve a **system of linear equations** by adding or subtracting them to remove one variable.

Linear Equations in Two Variables

Equations of the form ax + by = c, where a, b, and c are constants and x, y are unknowns.

Substitution Method

Solving one equation for one variable and **substituting** that expression into the other equation.

questions.question: The average of 8 numbers is 16. The average of 6 of these numbers is 16. The average of the remaining two numbers is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If the **average** of a **subset** (6 numbers) is equal to the **total average** (16), then the **remaining numbers** must also have the same average to maintain the balance.

Total average = 16

Subset (6) average = 16 ⇒ Deviation = 0

Average of remaining 2 numbers = Total Average + (Net Deviation ÷ 2) = 16 + 0 = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total numbers (nₜₒₜₐₗ) = 8

Average of 8 numbers (Aₜₒₜₐₗ) = 16

Numbers in first group (n₁) = 6

Average of 6 numbers (A₁) = 16

**Formula Used:**

Sum = Average × Number of observations

Average of remaining = (Total Sum − Sum of known group) ÷ Remaining count

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0e835ef5e90eccb6a1c866a8717d40164696aecd955e2b0de19eaef033bcfe1f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total sum of 8 numbers = 8 × 16 = 128

⇒ Sum of the first 6 numbers = 6 × 16 = 96

⇒ Sum of the **remaining two numbers** = 128 − 96 = 32

⇒ **Average** of the remaining two numbers = 32 ÷ 2 = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

The combined average of two groups is given by A꜀ₒₘbᵢₙₑd = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Rule

The sum of deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero (Σ(xᵢ − A) = 0).

Property of Constant Average

If a number equal to the average is added or removed from a data set, the average remains unchanged.</p

questions.question: Which of the following physiographic regions lies north of the Narmada River?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malwa Plateau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Malwa Plateau** lies to the north of the Narmada River, extending over parts of Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.
 
• It is bounded by the Aravalli range in the northwest and the Vindhya range in the south.
 
• The plateau is characterized by black soil, which is highly suitable for cotton cultivation and other crops.
 
• It forms a part of the Deccan Traps, created by extensive volcanic activity during the Cretaceous period.
 
• The Malwa Plateau also serves as a transition zone between the northern plains and the Deccan Plateau.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narmada River**

 
 
• The Narmada River flows westward and is one of the major rivers of peninsular India.
 
• It forms the traditional boundary between North and South India.
 
• The river originates from the **Amarkantak Plateau** in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The Narmada Valley is known for its rich biodiversity and fertile alluvial soils.
 
 
 
• **Deccan Plateau**
 
 
• The Deccan Plateau is a large plateau located south of the Narmada River.
 
• It is bounded by the Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, and the Satpura range.
 
• This region is known for its basaltic rock formations due to ancient volcanic activity.
 
 
 
• **Vindhya Range**
 
 
• The Vindhya Range runs parallel to the Narmada River and acts as a natural barrier between North and South India.
 
• It is not a continuous range but rather a series of discontinuous hills and ridges.
 
 
 
• **Physiographic Regions of India**
 
 
• India is divided into six physiographic regions: The Northern Mountains, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains, and Islands.
 
• The Malwa Plateau is a part of the Peninsular Plateau, which is the largest physiographic division of India.

questions.question: Consider a scenario where a user is interacting with a virtual reality (VR) environment. Which of the following input devices is least likely to be the primary means of navigation and interaction within this immersive environment?

options.text: Optical mouse connected to the computer
Head-mounted display with integrated motion tracking

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Optical mouse connected to the computer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An **optical mouse** is primarily designed for 2D navigation on flat surfaces, making it unsuitable for immersive 3D environments such as VR.
 
• VR environments rely on devices that provide spatial tracking and interaction within a 3D space, such as **handheld controllers** or **haptic gloves**.
 
• An optical mouse lacks the capability to track movements in a full 3D space, as it is confined to detecting surface motion in 2D.
 
• Devices like **head-mounted displays (HMDs)** with motion tracking and handheld controllers are the preferred tools for VR navigation and interaction.
 
• In contrast, an optical mouse is better suited for traditional desktop setups rather than immersive and dynamic environments like VR.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Handheld Controllers with Positional Tracking:**

 
 
• These are the most common input devices in VR, offering precise control and interactivity.
 
• They use sensors to track movements in 3D space, enabling natural navigation and object manipulation.
 
 
 
• **Head-Mounted Displays (HMDs):**
 
 
• HMDs are worn on the head and provide an immersive visual experience by displaying stereoscopic 3D graphics.
 
• Most HMDs include integrated motion tracking to adjust the view based on the user's head movements.
 
 
 
• **Haptic Gloves:**
 
 
• Haptic gloves are designed to provide tactile feedback, simulating the sense of touch in VR environments.
 
• They allow users to interact with virtual objects in a more realistic and intuitive manner.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Optical Mouse in VR:**
 
 
• An optical mouse is limited to surface-based 2D navigation and lacks 6 degrees of freedom (6DoF).
 
• It cannot provide immersive or precise interactions required in VR applications.
 
 
 
• **Importance of 6 Degrees of Freedom (6DoF):**
 
 
• 6DoF refers to the ability to track movements in three axes: forward/backward, up/down, left/right, along with pitch, yaw, and roll.
 
• Devices with 6DoF allow for a fully immersive experience, which is essential in VR environments.

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 12 hours. Another pipe can empty the filled tank in 24 hours. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, then the time (in hours) in which the tank will be two-third filled, is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net efficiency = **1/12 − 1/24 = 1/24** units per hour.

Time for full tank = **24 hours**.

Time for 2/3 filled = **24 × 2/3 = 16 hours**.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling Pipe **(A) = 12 hours**, Emptying Pipe **(B) = 24 hours**.

 **Pipe**
 **Time (Hours)**
 **Total Work (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**

 Pipe A (Inlet)
 12
 24 Units
 +2

 Pipe B (Outlet)
 24
 −1

**Calculations:**

⇒ Combined Efficiency of (A + B) = **2 − 1 = 1 unit/hour**.

⇒ Target Work = 2/3 of Total Work = **2/3 × 24 = 16 units**.

⇒ Time taken = Target Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = **16 ÷ 1 = 16 hours**.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Net Work Done

When one pipe fills and another empties, net work per hour = **1/x − 1/y**, where x is filling time and y is emptying time.

Efficiency Concept

Inlet pipes have **positive efficiency** while outlet (leakage) pipes have **negative efficiency**.

Fractional Work

To find time for a specific fraction of work, multiply the **total time** by that **fraction**.</p

questions.question: The mean proportional between 12 + 3sqrt(4) and 16 - 4sqrt(4) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Simplify terms: 12 + 3√4 = 12 + 3 × 2 = 18.

Simplify terms: 16 − 4√4 = 16 − 4 × 2 = 8.

Mean Proportional = √(18 × 8) = √144 = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e674564411a04730d98e2e32c08bac80a7c7df8d4a2a2d4db8ab3c263dad6b05.png] 

**Given:** First value (a) = 12 + 3√4, Second value (b) = 16 − 4√4

**Formula Used:** Mean proportional of **a** and **b** = √(a × b)

⇒ a = 12 + 3(2) = 12 + 6 = 18

⇒ b = 16 − 4(2) = 16 − 8 = 8

⇒ Mean Proportional = √(18 × 8)

⇒ Mean Proportional = √144

⇒ Mean Proportional = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

**__Additional Information__**

Third Proportional

The third proportional of two numbers **a** and **b** is defined as **c** such that a : b = b : c, given by c = b² / a.

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers **a**, **b**, and **c**, the fourth proportional **d** is such that a : b = c : d, calculated as d = (b × c) / a.

Continued Proportion

Three quantities **a**, **b**, **c** are in continued proportion if a/b = b/c, which implies b² = ac.</p

questions.question: ’Top-khanah’ was the general name given to the military/artillery branch of which of the following?

__
 
• The term 'Top-khanah' refers to the **artillery branch** of the Mughal military system, which played a crucial role in the empire's military campaigns.
 
• The Mughal emperors, especially **Babur and Akbar**, emphasized the use of artillery in warfare, giving the dynasty a strategic advantage over their adversaries.
 
• The Mughal artillery included **cannons, mortars, and matchlocks**, which were considered advanced military technology during their time.
 
• 'Top-khanah' was not just a term for the artillery itself but also referred to the **department responsible for manufacturing, storing, and maintaining** these weapons.
 
• The Mughal military system integrated artillery with their infantry and cavalry, marking a shift towards modern warfare in the Indian subcontinent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Babur's Role in Artillery Development**

 
 
• The first significant use of artillery in India was by Babur in the **First Battle of Panipat (1526)**, where his use of cannons helped defeat Ibrahim Lodi.
 
• Babur employed Ottoman gunpowder technology, which was brought to India by his skilled artillerymen like Ustad Ali and Mustafa.
 
 
 
• **Akbar's Military Reforms**
 
 
• Emperor Akbar established a dedicated **Top-khanah department** to improve the organization and efficiency of the Mughal artillery.
 
• Akbar's artillery innovations included the production of lightweight, mobile cannons to enhance battlefield maneuverability.
 
 
 
• **Artillery in Mughal Warfare**
 
 
• The Mughal artillery was categorized into **heavy artillery** (large cannons for sieges) and **light artillery** (smaller, more mobile guns for field battles).
 
• It played a vital role in major Mughal campaigns such as the conquest of Gujarat, Bengal, and the Deccan.
 
 
 
• **Decline of Mughal Artillery**
 
 
• By the 18th century, the Mughal artillery's effectiveness declined due to a lack of innovation and maintenance.
 
• European colonial powers like the British and French outpaced the Mughals with superior artillery technology.

• The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution provides for special administrative arrangements for tribal areas in the states of **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram** located in North-East India.

questions.question: The LCM of 44, 86 and another number, x, is 7568. Which of the following can be the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check **divisibility** of options: the **LCM** must be divisible by every number in the set.

Given **LCM** = 7568. Let us check the options for divisibility.

Option (1) 176: 7568 ÷ 176 = 43 (Divisible)

Option (2) 145: Ends in 5, but 7568 does not end in 0 or 5 (Not Divisible)

Option (3) 101: 7568 ÷ 101 ≈ 74.93 (Not Divisible)

Option (4) 165: 165 is a multiple of 5, but 7568 is not (Not Divisible)

**∴ The correct answer is 176.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers are 44, 86, and **x**. **LCM** = 7568.

**Formula Used:** **Prime Factorization** method for LCM.

⇒ Prime factorization of 44 = 2² × 11

⇒ Prime factorization of 86 = 2 × 43

⇒ Prime factorization of 7568 = 2⁴ × 11 × 43 = 16 × 11 × 43

⇒ Since the **LCM** contains 2⁴ (which is 16), and neither 44 nor 86 contains 2⁴, the number **x** must contribute 2⁴ to the LCM.

⇒ **x** must be a multiple of 16 (2⁴).

⇒ Checking options for multiples of 16:

⇒ 176 = 16 × 11 (Multiple of 16)

⇒ 145, 101, 165 are not multiples of 16.

⇒ Also, 176 = 2⁴ × 11, which fits the **Prime Factorization** of the **LCM**.

**∴ The correct answer is 176.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Definition

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** is the smallest positive integer that is divisible by each of the numbers in a given set.

LCM and HCF Relationship

For two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM**: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

Prime Factorization Method

To find **LCM**, take the highest power of each prime factor present in the **prime factorization** of the given numbers.</p

questions.question: A person drove at 77 km/hr for 3.5 hours, then increased his speed by 9 km/hr, and reached the destination in another hour. Find the average speed (in km/hr) of the person during the entire journey.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ 
**Initial speed** = 77 km/hr for 3.5 hours.
 
**New speed** = 77 + 9 = 86 km/hr for 1 hour.
 
**Deviation method**: Taking 77 as base average speed.
 
**Net deviation** = (86 − 77) × 1 hour = +9 km.
 
**Average increase** = 9 ÷ (3.5 + 1) = 9 ÷ 4.5 = 2 km/hr.
 
**Final average speed** = 77 + 2 = 79 km/hr.
 
**∴ The correct answer is 79 km/hr.**
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**
 
**Speed 1 (S₁)** = 77 km/hr | **Time 1 (T₁)** = 3.5 hours
 
**Speed 2 (S₂)** = 77 + 9 = 86 km/hr | **Time 2 (T₂)** = 1 hour
 
**Formula Used:**
 
**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time
 
**Calculations:**
 
⇒ Distance 1 = 77 × 3.5 = 269.5 km
 
⇒ Distance 2 = 86 × 1 = 86 km
 
⇒ Total Distance = 269.5 + 86 = 355.5 km
 
⇒ Total Time = 3.5 + 1 = 4.5 hours
 
⇒ Average Speed = 355.5 ÷ 4.5
 
⇒ Average Speed = 3555 ÷ 45 = 79 km/hr
 
**∴ The correct answer is 79 km/hr.**
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**
 
Weighted Average Speed
 
When different speeds are maintained for different durations, Average Speed = (S₁T₁ + S₂T₂) ÷ (T₁ + T₂).
 
Equal Distance Formula
 
If two equal distances are covered at speeds S₁ and S₂, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).
 
Relative Speed
 
Same direction speed = S₁ − S₂; Opposite direction speed = S₁ + S₂.</p

questions.question: For a regular polygon, the sum of the interior angles is 200% more than the sum of its exterior angles. Each interior angle of the polygon measures x°. What is the value of x?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **interior angles** = 3 × Sum of **exterior angles** (since 200% more means 100% + 200% = 300%).

(n − 2) × 180° = 3 × 360°

n − 2 = (3 × 360) ÷ 180 ⇒ n − 2 = 6 ⇒ n = 8 (**Octagon**).

Each **exterior angle** = 360° ÷ 8 = 45°.

Each **interior angle** (x) = 180° − 45° = 135°.

**∴ The correct answer is 135°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

2. Sum of **exterior angles** of any polygon = 360°

3. Each **interior angle** of a regular polygon = (Sum of interior angles) ÷ n

⇒ Sum of **exterior angles** = 360°

⇒ Sum of **interior angles** = 360° + (200 ÷ 100) × 360°

⇒ Sum of **interior angles** = 360° + 720° = 1080°

⇒ (n − 2) × 180° = 1080°

⇒ n − 2 = 1080° ÷ 180°

⇒ n − 2 = 6

⇒ n = 8

⇒ Each **interior angle** (x) = 1080° ÷ 8

⇒ x = 135°

**∴ The correct answer is 135°.**

__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the given data in **ascending order**: 15, 19, 26, 46, 53, 72, 80, 82, 86, 87, 91.

Count the number of observations (**n**) = 11.

Since **n** is **odd**, the **Median** is the middle term.

Middle term = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term = **6th term**.

The 6th term in the sorted list is **72**.

**∴ The correct answer is 72.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Data = 46, 19, 87, 72, 80, 91, 82, 15, 53, 86, 26

Median for Even Number of Observations

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a thermometric property?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Colour of a substance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A thermometric property is any physical property that changes measurably with temperature and can be used for temperature measurement.
 
• **Colour of a substance** is not considered a thermometric property as it does not have a predictable or consistent relationship with temperature for accurate measurement.
 
• Examples of thermometric properties include **pressure, volume, length, electrical resistance, and thermal expansion**, which are commonly used in various thermometers.
 
• Properties such as pressure and electrical resistance are widely applied in devices like gas thermometers and resistance temperature detectors (RTDs).
 
• Colour changes with temperature (e.g., in some materials) are not precise enough to serve as a reliable thermometric property in practical applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thermometric Properties:**

 
 
• These are physical properties of matter that change in a predictable and measurable way with temperature.
 
• Examples include thermal expansion (length or volume), pressure of a gas, and electrical resistance.
 
• These properties are utilized in designing instruments like thermometers and pyrometers.
 
 
 
• **Common Thermometers:**
 
 
• Mercury-in-glass thermometers use the expansion of mercury as a thermometric property.
 
• Resistance thermometers (RTDs) use the change in electrical resistance of a conductor.
 
• Gas thermometers rely on the pressure of a fixed volume of gas as the thermometric property.
 
 
 
• **Why Colour is Not a Thermometric Property:**
 
 
• While some materials change colour with temperature (e.g., thermochromic materials), the change is not consistent or linear across all substances.
 
• Colour changes are not easily quantifiable in a manner suitable for precise temperature measurement.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Thermometric Properties:**
 
 
• Thermometric properties are used in both scientific and industrial settings for accurate temperature monitoring and control.
 
• Examples include clinical thermometers, industrial sensors, and meteorological equipment.

Identify the class with the highest frequency: **20-30** has the maximum frequency of **35**.

Use the grouped mode formula: Mode = L + [(f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h

Substitute L = 20, f₁ = 35, f₀ = 29, f₂ = 25, h = 10.

Mode = 20 + [(35 − 29) ÷ (70 − 54)] × 10 = 20 + 3.75 = 23.75 years.

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Frequency distribution of ages of patients.

Maximum frequency is **35**, which corresponds to the class interval **20-30**.

**Formula Used:**

Mode of grouped data is given by:

Mode = L + [ (f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) ] × h

Where:

L = Lower limit of the modal class

f₁ = Frequency of the modal class

f₀ = Frequency of the class preceding the modal class

f₂ = Frequency of the class succeeding the modal class

h = Width of the class interval

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e7471fecc1c292ba0998f460f24b778943d36122ef23004d6a7b4ebb2a810cc.png] 

**Calculations:**

From the given data, the modal class is **20-30** because it has the highest frequency of **35**.

⇒ L = 20

⇒ f₁ = 35

⇒ f₀ = 29

⇒ f₂ = 25

⇒ h = 30 − 20 = 10

Substituting these values into the formula:

⇒ Mode = 20 + [ (35 − 29) ÷ (2 × 35 − 29 − 25) ] × 10

⇒ Mode = 20 + [ 6 ÷ (70 − 54) ] × 10

⇒ Mode = 20 + [ 6 ÷ 16 ] × 10

⇒ Mode = 20 + 0.375 × 10

⇒ Mode = 20 + 3.75

⇒ Mode = 23.75 years

⇒ **Option (2) 6.56** is incorrect as it lies completely outside the range of the given data classes.

⇒ **Option (4) 22.58** is incorrect due to calculation errors in the frequency differences.

**∴ The correct answer is 23.75 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Median of Grouped Data

Median = L + [ (N/2 − CF) ÷ f ] × h, where L is the lower limit of the median class, CF is the cumulative frequency of the preceding class, f is the frequency of the median class, and h is the class width.

Mean of Grouped Data (Direct Method)

Mean = Σ(fᵢ × xᵢ) ÷ Σfᵢ, where xᵢ is the class mark (midpoint) of each class interval and fᵢ is the corresponding frequency.</p

questions.question: If the fourth proportion to P, 4 and 3 is 6, then find the value of P.

For four numbers to be in proportion, the product of extremes equals the product of means.

P × 6 = 4 × 3

6P = 12 ⇒ P = 2

The numbers are **P**, **4**, **3**, and the fourth proportion is **6**.

**Formula Used:**

If a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a : b :: c : d), then:

a ÷ b = c ÷ d ⇒ a × d = b × c

**Calculations:**

⇒ P ÷ 4 = 3 ÷ 6

⇒ P × 6 = 4 × 3

⇒ 6P = 12

⇒ P = 12 ÷ 6

If two numbers a and b are in continued proportion (a : b :: b : c), then the third proportion c is calculated as c = b² ÷ a.

Mean Proportion

questions.question: Rati travels from City A to City B. If Rati drives her car at 1/3 of her normal speed, then she reaches City B 50 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Rati would take to travel from City A to City B if she drove at her normal speed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **distance** is constant, **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time**.

Speed ratio = 3 : 1 → Time ratio = 1 : 3.

Difference in time ratio = 3 − 1 = 2 units → 50 minutes.

1 unit = 25 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5cb6c2bd4c8679dbbe5acccf1ccea7c697c5895c19f51894e0725ec051138c03.png] 

**Given:** Reduced speed = 1/3 of normal speed, Time delay = 50 minutes.

**Formula Used:** Time = Distance ÷ Speed (Time ∝ 1/Speed when distance is constant).

⇒ Let normal speed be S and normal time be T.

⇒ New speed = S/3, so New time = 3T.

⇒ 3T − T = 50 minutes.

⇒ 2T = 50 minutes.

⇒ T = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion Rule

If speed becomes a/b of original speed, the new time becomes b/a of original time, provided distance remains the same.

Average Speed

For two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

In the same direction, speed is subtracted (u − v). In opposite directions, speed is added (u + v).</p

__Shortcut Trick__

Area of a quadrilateral = (1/2) × Diagonal × (Sum of perpendiculars from opposite vertices)

Let the diagonal be AC, and the perpendiculars be h₁ and h₂.

Area = (1/2) × AC × (h₁ + h₂)

⇒ 324 = (1/2) × AC × (12 + 15)

⇒ AC = (324 × 2) ÷ 27 = 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of perpendicular from B to AC (h₁) = 12 cm

Length of perpendicular from D to AC (h₂) = 15 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of quadrilateral ABCD = Area of ΔABC + Area of ΔADC

Area of a triangle = (1/2) × Base × Height

**Calculations:**

The diagonal AC divides the quadrilateral ABCD into two triangles, ΔABC and ΔADC.

⇒ Area of quadrilateral ABCD = Area of ΔABC + Area of ΔADC

⇒ Area of quadrilateral ABCD = ((1/2) × AC × BP₁) + ((1/2) × AC × DP₂)

⇒ 324 = ((1/2) × AC × 12) + ((1/2) × AC × 15)

⇒ 324 = (1/2) × AC × (12 + 15)

⇒ 324 = (1/2) × AC × 27

⇒ 324 = 13.5 × AC

⇒ AC = 324 ÷ 13.5

⇒ AC = 24 cm

**__Additional Information__**

Area of a General Quadrilateral

The area of any quadrilateral with a diagonal d and perpendicular offsets h₁ and h₂ from the opposite vertices is given by Area = (1/2) × d × (h₁ + h₂).

Area of a Cyclic Quadrilateral (Brahmagupta's Formula)

For a cyclic quadrilateral with sides a, b, c, and d, the area is given by √((s − a)(s − b)(s − c)(s − d)), where s is the semi-perimeter: s = (a + b + c + d) ÷ 2.

Area of a Rhombus

The area of a rhombus with diagonals d₁ and d₂ is given by Area = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂, since the diagonals bisect each other at right angles.</p
